From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, samir@finplus.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Increased 429/5xx from Redwood API since 11/13 07:45 — urgent

Ben / Samir —

Initial triage (logs attached):
- We see a sudden rise in 429s and 5xxs originating from the same client token (FP-prod-token-**).
- Error rate: 429s climbed to 18% of requests between 07:45–08:10 PT; 5xxs peaked at ~3.1%.
- Many requests share identical request_id headers and stair-stepped timestamps — indicative of tight retry loops.

Suspected cause: client-side retry logic without jitter / exponential backoff has interacted with our rate limiter, producing a feedback loop. We’ve pulled the host-level traces and included a sample in logs.tar.gz.

Short mitigation suggestions we can enact now:
1) Temporarily increase the token-level burst allowance for FP while we work through root cause — reduces immediate failures.
2) Apply a soft throttle (5 requests/sec) on the offending route for that token to stop amplification.
3) Coordinate with FinPlus to patch the client SDK to add randomized exponential backoff and limit retries.

I’ll start with (1) and (2) pending approval from Ben.

Monica
Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: logs.tar.gz (text/plain archive)]

Monica —

Thanks for the quick triage. We discovered that one of our recent client releases (v3.4.1) changed the SDK default retry behavior: retries are now aggressive (5 immediate retries, no jitter) for idempotent routes. We shipped it to 30% of traffic this morning and rolled to 100% at ~07:40 PT. That matches the spike timing.

Attached is a code snippet from the SDK config (excerpt):

// FinPlus SDK client config
const client = new FPClient({
  retryPolicy: { retries: 5, backoffMs: 100, jitter: 0 } // default in v3.4.1
});

We can roll back the SDK immediately or ship a hotfix to add exponential backoff + jitter. Please proceed with whatever reduces customer impact fastest. We’ll also whitelist any temporary allowance under strict monitoring.

—Samir

Subject: Post-incident update and next steps (FP incident 2026-11-13)

Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the rapid coordination last week. Quick summary of what we did and next steps:

What happened:
- FinPlus v3.4.1 changed SDK defaults to aggressive immediate retries (5x, no jitter) and was rolled to 100% traffic ~07:40 PT on 11/13.
- That client pattern interacted with our per-token rate limiter causing a feedback loop — 429s rose to ~18% and 5xxs to ~3% for a ~30 minute window.

Mitigations applied (completed):
- Token-level burst increased for FP for 40 minutes to reduce customer-visible failures.
- Soft per-route throttle applied to dissipate amplification and prevent cross-customer tail impact.
- FP rolled a hotfix to their SDK (v3.4.2) adding exponential backoff + randomized jitter; we validated a downstream drop in retries.
- We pushed a temporary rule to monitoring to alert on identical-request-timestamp patterns.

Artifacts attached: sdk-backoff-fix.diff, postmortem-1pager.md.

Next actions (owners / ETA):
- Redwood SDK / docs team to publish a backoff best-practice guide and update ours to safe defaults (Steph / 2026-11-19).
- Support & SRE to add an auto-mitigation policy for token-level throttles when retry amplification signatures are detected (Monica / 2026-11-22).
- Customer success: follow up with FP execs and confirm SLA credits status (Marissa / 2026-11-18).

If this is acceptable, we’ll file the full postmortem and schedule a follow-up readout with FP on 11/19.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
